title: Khalsa Conduct and the Lion Cave Episode Begins

blocks.text: The page continues its portrait of persecuted Khalsa life by showing that the Singhs hide by day and move by night, refusing to surrender initiative even when heavily outnumbered. Their survival is presented not as passive concealment but as a disciplined rhythm of stealth, endurance, and sudden action against Mughal camps.

From that wider description the narrative narrows into a specific ordeal, introducing the tale of Singhs who must take shelter in a lion's cave near Mirankot. Laddha Singh emerges as the central name in this setting, and the new sub-episode begins to translate collective Khalsa conduct into one intense local test.

The transition matters because it shows how general persecution produced improvised refuges and legends of defiance. The Singhs remain under pressure on every side, yet the story insists that hardship only sharpened their courage and mutual loyalty.
